coverage.objective: Scheme entry 6: nutrient cycling in nature

evidence.locator: block 7 (sha256 c2c9d6de15c9e85f2424f85a328436ae6ff161dbde8bde99962005840f02280e); heading block 782 (sha256 3bf73e7e62ad294a58a3f408d5b7a71ee63e86c0473df26d1eb449ba327ae50c); definition block 783 (sha256 daa620280a5f71981116d809fd3df7b4e76e87fdcca4aaaf3c1bf5fda2a68282)
evidence.explanation: The scheme gives one entry, 'Week 6 - Nutrient cycling in Nature'. The heading repeats it and block 783 defines a nutrient cycle as the circulation of nutrients such as carbon, sulphur and water. The week then teaches the carbon and water cycles only; the sulphur example is not developed (see COV-BIO-T1-W06-SULPHUR).

evidence.locator: carbon cycle blocks 784-803 (range sha256 8bec1554dfa9d9c51a5497ace59e3081808cce34dfb384d33ffa22c8b72c9500); definition block 785 (sha256 0045951d0b5ae6bc7527db143932eaf5b1d867e43bc0b5b930aee4f53a92cdef); processes blocks 786-790; importance blocks 791-795
evidence.explanation: The carbon cycle is defined at 785 as the use and return of carbon(IV) oxide, with photosynthesis, respiration, putrefaction and combustion named. Each process is taught at 786-789, sea-atmosphere exchange at 790, and four importance points at 792-795. The cycle image at block 795 (media/image6.jpeg) has its own disposition item, BIO-VIS-T1-NUTRIENT-CYCLES.

evidence.locator: water cycle blocks 804-825 (range sha256 2216c6958a8a91fe4d04ba12a95415986d519fec0f3f14faeca354dbb081239e); definition block 805 (sha256 9b7b5c4038e4e42a0632d0276cb9d4a45cfa3c2c5ce5a7e70a9ebc9932d404cb); importance to plants blocks 806-812; importance to animals blocks 813-819; water-cycle image block 821
evidence.explanation: The water cycle is defined at 805 through evaporation and condensation, with plant absorption, transpiration, animal use, run-off, percolation, underground water and ocean return described. Six importance points for plants (806-812) and seven for animals (813-819) follow. The cycle image at block 821 (media/image7.jpeg) has its own disposition item, BIO-VIS-T1-NUTRIENT-CYCLES. The source prints 'transportation' for transpiration at 805 and 807; that is recorded, not corrected.

coverage.objective: The ordered sequence of steps the week says the scientific process runs through

evidence.locator: block 27 (sha256 6f85d0af621f25a53e3b94e1fceade1b03df4de8a6d5f9e9a9f30257621ac42a); blocks 29-31
evidence.explanation: Block 27 lists the order: 'Scientific process begins with observation, followed by classification, inference, measurement, identification, hypothesis, experiment, control or conclusion, theory law or principle.' Only three of those steps are then defined in the week - observation (29), hypothesis (30) and experiment (31) - so the list is taught as a sequence to recite rather than as steps the learner is shown. 'control or conclusion' is written as one step, and the closing three words carry no separators ('theory law or principle').

evidence.locator: backend/src/db/ss1/subjects/biology.json lessons[] length 0; importer not run
evidence.explanation: The sequence is present in the source with no deliverable lesson. PARTIAL; the steps the list promises but never defines are indexed separately as COV-BIO-T1-W01-PROCESS-GAP (UNRESOLVED).

coverage.objective: Observation, hypothesis and experiment defined, and the parts of an experiment: aim, apparatus/materials, method or procedure, result, conclusion

evidence.explanation: Observation (29) is 'the use of human senses to describe an observation by using the characteristics and properties of material', with the same block pointing on from observation to classification, inference, measurement and identification. Hypothesis (30) is 'a sensible proposal or reasonable assumption or a scientific guess that can be subjected to verification or being tested'. Experiment (31) is 'the process used for testing of hypothesis through experimentation during which data are collected', which defines the thing in terms of itself.

The parts of an experiment are given one line each: AIM (33) 'the purpose for which the experiment is carried out'; APPARATUS//MATERIALS (34) 'the materials that will be used for the experiment'; METHOD or PROCEDURE (35) 'used to describe the details that are required step by step'; RESULT (36) 'the record of what is seen during and after the experiment'; CONCLUSION (37) 'used to finalize the outcome of the whole experiment'. They are numbered (iv)-(viii), continuing the (i)-(iii) of blocks 29-31, so the source presents the parts of an experiment as peers of observation, hypothesis and experiment itself. No experiment, apparatus list, quantity or safety instruction is given anywhere in blocks 13-41; the first experiments with materials in this document are the Week 5 experiments I-V at blocks 714-765, and this item invents none.

'classification' occurs at blocks 4, 27, 29, 134, 135, 156, 188, 248, 249, 261 and 278: blocks 4, 134-278 are the Week 3 taxonomy teaching (scheme line 'Week 3 -Classification of Living things', block 4, sha256 90846288953e56236069142972ddfd5b1db1e76a5d61e83007ecc1f7af34b813), not the process step, so the step is named at 27 and 29 and never taught as a process step.

evidence.locator: whole-document text search for the string "control"; blocks 575, 620, 744, 974, 1052
evidence.explanation: 'control' occurs fifteen times in the document. Besides block 27, the hits are pest and disease control (blocks 573-579, 617, 620), the wording of a Week 5 experiment (722, 744), abiotic factors (974) and a hormone function (1052). No block teaches a control as a scientific-process step, and the source's own phrasing 'control or conclusion' (27) merges two different ideas into one item. coverage.objective: How a hypothesis is tested and becomes a theory, and how the source says a theory becomes a law or principle

evidence.explanation: Block 38 makes the end of the experiment the test of the hypothesis: if later experiments show it false the idea 'is then repeated or rejected', and 'when the hypothesis is true after several repeated experiment it is accepted and becomes a THEORY'.

evidence.locator: block 40 (sha256 50188a7f28f8dcac90ac3da602d1a481fe920f8ec95855ccf27036acf7a71689)
evidence.explanation: Block 40 defines a THEORY as 'a tested hypothesis that has been confirmed to be true' and states that 'By the time the theory is extensively tested and proven to be true, it becomes a LAW OR PRINCIPLE'. This item records that wording and does not correct it; whether the escalation of a confirmed theory into a law is what the curriculum requires is the factual question held by BIOLOGY-T1-W01-THEORY-LAW-FACT and BIO-FACT-T1-W01-SCOPE. The words 'theory', 'law' and 'hypothesis' occur in this document only at blocks 27, 30, 31, 38 and 40, so there is no other passage to check the claim against.
